policy: Compare algorithm/data-flow/asymptotic responsibilities, not browser-vs-WinUI implementation technology or raw cross-language wall-clock numbers.

referenceFacts: applyEdits validates/sorts edits and applies descending to the piece tree
very large edit sets are reduced instead of blindly applying thousands of overlapping temporary edits
one projection object is stored per model line
a prefix-sum structure maps model-line projection counts to global view-line identities
single-line changes replace one projection and update one prefix value
structural model-line insertions splice the outer projection array and prefix values
decorations are queried through interval-search structures rather than full-list scans per visible line
bindings are indexed by first chord
candidate/context resolution searches the first-chord bucket
matching candidates are examined from highest precedence toward lower precedence

acceptedPlatformDifferences.difference: Win2D/DirectWrite command-list ViewParts replace DOM/browser view parts.
acceptedPlatformDifferences.acceptance: Allowed when dirty-layer boundaries and visible-work asymptotics remain bounded.

acceptedPlatformDifferences.difference: Windows TSF ITextStoreACP2/ITfKeystrokeMgr replaces browser textarea/EditContext integration.
acceptedPlatformDifferences.acceptance: Platform adaptation; Monaco model/selection/undo responsibilities remain authoritative.

acceptedPlatformDifferences.difference: The outer per-model-line projection vector can move suffix slots on model-line insertion/deletion.
acceptedPlatformDifferences.acceptance: Matches Monaco 0.57 modelLineProjections array splice complexity shape; unchanged view-line payloads are not globally renumbered/rebuilt.

acceptedPlatformDifferences.difference: Native C++/DirectWrite wall-clock numbers are not compared numerically to JS/browser timings.
acceptedPlatformDifferences.acceptance: Release gates use deterministic work counts and asymptotic behavior; wall-clock is trend evidence only.
